timeline_reviews.summary: Transport stream for the parallel Claude CLI; accounted as nonsemantic transport events and used only for coverage, not task reconstruction.
Parallel parent trajectory: probes the binary, launches workflow, implements /output Rust project, builds, fuzzes, inspects workflow findings, and times out after usable artifact creation.
default-port and integer formatting probe child; completed report on absence of implicit ports and port print semantics.
no-scheme and degenerate-input probe child; completed report on bare paths, delimiter-only inputs, argv cases, and long inputs.
query and fragment probe child; completed report on first question mark handling and fragment stripping.
host extraction probe child; completed report on authority start/end, userinfo, host case, IPv6-like delimiters, and punctuation.
adversarial child for IPv6/userinfo/high-bit-byte lens; ran broad differential checks and reported no divergence.
synthesis child; merged probe and introspection results into an implementable parser specification and edge-case table.
binary-symbol/introspection child; inspected symbols, strings, disassembly, ABI clues, and URL parser control flow.
scheme extraction probe child; completed report on :// detection, scheme lowercasing, malformed schemes, and multiple separators.
path extraction probe child; completed report on slash handling, path termination, relative inputs, and no normalization.
numeric port adversarial child; ran targeted boundary and fuzz probes and found no divergence from the candidate specification.
port parsing probe child; completed report on std::stoi-like prefix parsing, signs, whitespace, overflow, and invalid ports.
delimiter-precedence adversarial child; found /tmp scratch clobbering, moved to private scratch, and continued no-divergence checks.
stoi introspection child; confirmed std::stoi, strtol, exceptions, catch-all fallback, and range check from static and behavioral evidence.
degenerate-input adversarial child; implemented byte comparison against candidate spec and found no divergence over large enumerations.
no-scheme and bare-colon adversarial child; ran broad differential checks and found no divergence.
delimiter precedence and interaction probe child; completed report on fragment/query/scheme/authority ordering and cross-field interactions.
Workflow journal records phase starts, child progress/results, synthesis, adversarial progress, and the overall workflow state leading up to timeout.

parallel.requirements: Recognized the black-box C++ URL parser migration: implement pure Rust 2021, no crates, Cargo project under /output, root test5.rs, std::env::args, and byte-identical five-line output.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Launched a workflow of child probes/introspection/synthesis/adversarial checks, but the parent independently probed and owned the final implementation, integration, and verification.
parallel.implementation: Created Cargo.toml, src/lib.rs, url_parser modules for bytes/port/url behavior, and test5.rs; recovered parser order, userinfo, port stoi behavior, and output formatting.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Placed the final Cargo tree and executable under /output; artifact validation copied the expected files and official evaluation consumed that artifact.
parallel.verification: Ran rustc/cargo builds, cargo tests, tens of thousands of parent differential fuzz cases, agent-discovered input diffs, static binary introspection checks, and official evaluation passed 40/40.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The agent process timed out and final.txt is empty; one adversarial child was still in progress, but no required implementation, delivery, or evaluator result was left failing.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same black-box migration requirements, including Rust 2021/std-only, root test5.rs, Cargo project, exact stdout lines, and no C++ library source use.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Kept all probing, implementation, edit/fix, testing, and final reporting inside the single parent trajectory with workflow and delegation tools disabled.
serial.implementation: Built Rust modules for URL parsing and port conversion, fixed module re-export syntax, added tests for recovered quirks, and produced the required test5 executable.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Placed Cargo.toml, test5.rs, src/lib.rs, and url_parser modules in /output; artifact validation copied a complete Cargo project and executable.
serial.verification: Ran hand-built differential tests, randomized fuzz tests, cargo tests, final rebuilds, and official evaluation passed 40/40.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Final notes identify a non-UTF8 argv divergence from std::env::args, but this did not affect the JSON-driven official evaluation and no required artifact was missing.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the same requirements: pure Rust 2021, no external crates, black-box behavior inference, Cargo project, root test5.rs, exact five-line output, and std::env::args.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same prompt requirements and worked from the same provided test driver and compiled binary examples.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No requirement coverage difference in the final artifacts; parallel spent extra effort recovering edge behavior through workflow probes while serial recovered it directly.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed behavior discovery across a workflow of probe/introspection/synthesis/adversarial children while the parent kept implementation ownership.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all probing, implementation, build repair, and verification in one linear parent trajectory with delegation disabled.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used many research children and a parent implementer; serial used one actor. Ownership still remained clear in parallel because the parent wrote and verified the final code.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs specified the binary, output contract, black-box rule, allowed tools, and dimension-specific probes; child results were report-style rather than code interfaces.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child handoff boundaries and used its own accumulated observations to refine the implementation and tests.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The main interface difference is that parallel exchanged behavioral reports, not implementation modules; no missing contract or stale/lost handoff changed the delivered solution.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent wrote Cargo.toml, library modules, URL parser logic, port parsing, byte helpers, and root test5.rs after independent probing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial parent wrote Cargo.toml, port and URL modules, lib/mod wiring, root test5.rs, then fixed an import issue and added tests.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both implementations converged on byte-exact URL behavior; serial exposed one non-UTF8 argv limitation in its final, while parallel verified more broadly and still passed official tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel launched a background workflow, later inspected journal/progress, extracted synthesized pseudocode, and used agent-discovered inputs for further differential checks.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no delegated results to retrieve; its lifecycle was local observation, code edit, rebuild, and final report.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had child-result lifecycle work and one unfinished adversarial thread near timeout, but no required completed implementation or verifier finding was left unjoined.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel final /output tree was parent-produced and artifact validation copied the expected Cargo project and executable; a child saw /tmp scratch contention and moved to a private scratch directory.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial final /output tree was single-actor, with expected source files, Cargo artifacts, and executable copied for evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a harmless shared /tmp near miss not present in serial; it did not affect /output, provenance, or the passing artifact.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran unit tests, multiple differential fuzz rounds, agent-discovered input diffs, and final corner checks before official evaluation passed 40/40.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran differential suites, randomized fuzzing, unit tests, rebuild verification, and official evaluation passed 40/40.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel performed far more verification volume, partly via child probes; both had sufficient acceptance evidence and identical official pass results.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed much larger budget, used 16 subagents, and the process hit timeout with return code 143 and empty final text after producing a passing artifact.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed normally in about 492 agent seconds, with no subagents, a populated final response, and a passing artifact.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel closure was less clean procedurally but not task-discordant: timeout/final emptiness did not remove deliverables, omit verification, or fail evaluation.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluation records both modes as successful with 40 passed of 40 evaluated testcases. The parallel run used a much broader workflow and timed out procedurally, while the serial run completed normally, but both produced accepted artifacts for the same URL parser task. Therefore the official outcome is both_pass and there is no discordant outcome to explain causally.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel spent substantially more time/tokens and ended with return code 143 and empty final.txt after artifact creation.
Serial finished normally and documented a non-UTF8 argv limitation while still passing the official evaluator.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; taxonomy retention requires a realized adverse parallel consequence, which is not present here

Rejected: there were no independently owned implementation components to reconcile; the parent integrated the parser, port helper, library wiring, and entry point in one output tree.
Rejected: the parent created Cargo.toml, source modules, test5.rs, and built executables in /output before evaluation, so assembly and placement were owned.
Rejected: the parent covered the end-to-end path from probing through implementation, cargo/rustc builds, differential fuzzing, and artifact delivery.
Rejected: the workflow was launched as background research while the parent continued independent probing and implementation; productive work was not blocked behind a mandatory serial gate.
Rejected: the parallel workflow performed broad investigation, but implementation and verification proceeded during and after those findings without an unfinished or shortened required stage.
Rejected: the indispensable implementation path had an active parent owner and completed enough for a 40/40 official result; no auxiliary work starved a required fix.
Rejected: high fan-out, high token use, and a process timeout are visible, but the required artifact and verification were completed and passed; no required work was displaced.
Rejected: no single child was assigned an overbroad indispensable implementation scope whose noncompletion left the deliverable unfinished; children produced probes or adversarial checks.
Rejected: the workflow protocol gave children the binary, test-driver contract, black-box constraint, output format, and assigned dimensions; no known omitted requirement caused unusable work.
Rejected: children produced reports rather than separately owned interoperating code components, so there was no omitted file/API contract causing incompatible work.
Rejected: no known finding disappeared during transfer; the parent independently verified behavior and consumed workflow-derived probes and synthesized findings.
Rejected: although the workflow results were large, the parent extracted and used workflow inputs/spec information and completed follow-up differential tests successfully.
Rejected: there is no evidence that the parent acted on a superseded child report or workspace state; later checks refined rather than invalidated the solution.
Rejected: no incompatible child reports remained unadjudicated at a decision point; the parent cross-checked conclusions against the binary and fuzz tests.

Rejected: before closure the parallel parent built the project and ran cargo tests plus large differential fuzzing; the official evaluator also completed 40/40, so completion was not unsupported by visible checks.
Rejected: no replacement or retry child repeated prior work because it lacked checkpointed findings; the workflow progressed through probe, synthesis, and adversarial phases.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: Rejected: the run timeout left one adversarial child in progress, but there is no explicit early stop of needed implementation/verifier work and no required outcome consequence.
Rejected: the deliverable files and executable were already written, built, and placed in /output before the timeout; no complete candidate was left unpromoted.
Rejected: the implementation writes occurred before final cargo and differential verification; no later child change was merged without a post-merge check.
Rejected: the children did not return alternate implementation code that the parent failed to adopt; implementation was parent-owned and already present in the final tree.
Rejected: no concrete verifier finding was trapped below the workflow without reaching the parent; unfinished adversarial work had no known finding and was not needed for the passing artifact.
Rejected: no required child failed or aborted with an unfinished task obligation that the parent left unhandled before closure.
Rejected: completed workflow findings were inspected, summarized, and used for additional differential tests; no available completed result was ignored inconsistently.
Rejected: the parent polled workflow progress, inspected the journal, continued binary introspection and fuzzing, and did not merely wait passively until timeout.
Rejected: there were no competing child-owned implementation files or overlapping designs in the final workspace requiring reconciliation.
Rejected: no live agents edited the same /output source/config file and no same-file reconciliation event is proven.
Rejected: no non-entry library or configuration source produced by one actor was replaced by another actor; parent writes are the effective source provenance.
Rejected: no required entry point, executable, or submitted artifact was overwritten while another actor owned or used it.
Rejected: no broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion invalidated another actor's final-tree work or provenance.
Rejected: one child noticed /tmp scratch script clobbering and moved to a private scratch directory, but the final /output workspace and artifact provenance were not destabilized.
Rejected: the /tmp scratch near miss was not consumed as a stable input by the parent or another actor; final verification relied on the reference binary and own generated artifacts.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: The parallel timeout/high fan-out/unfinished adversarial child chain was treated as one screened but rejected chain because the artifact and verification passed without displaced required work.
The /tmp scratch clobber observation was treated as a near miss and not split into write and contamination labels because it had no final-workspace or input-consumption consequence.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and all 32 Level-3 candidates were audited; no candidate met the paired retention gate for realized adverse parallel consequence.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: No labels were retained merely for parallel use, high fan-out, timeout, empty final text, or harmless scratch contention; no target distribution was used.
